name: 1-(2-Dimethylaminoethyl)piperazine
description: 1-(2-Dimethylaminoethyl)piperazine (CAS 3644-18-6 ), also known commercially as TAP, is a bifunctional tertiary amine building block used in pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing. Its dual amine sites make it a reactive intermediate for constructing complex nitrogen-containing scaffolds in drug development pipelines. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, TAP serves as a key intermediate in synthesis. This is particularly true where piperazine-based structural motifs are required in the final molecule. Biotechnology researchers use it in the preparation of linkers and conjugates for targeted drug delivery systems. The compound also functions as a polymerization initiator or catalyst in specialty polymer formulations where controlled amine reactivity is required. In research-scale synthesis, it supports the development of libraries. These heterocyclic compound libraries are used in high-throughput screening programs. 1-(2-Dimethylaminoethyl)piperazine is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial purities, typically ranging from 97% to 99%+. Material is available in research quantities through to bulk industrial volumes to support both early-stage development and commercial manufacturing. Technical and high-purity grades are the most common. These are the most commonly sourced specifications in pharmaceutical and biotechnology procurement.
